newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 10.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- President Kim Young-sam, in statement during a luncheon with ministers of state on Thursday, said: "Strikes being held at industrial labour sites are disrupting social order and worsening the nation's economic hardships". He said he would deal with the situation sternly according to the law.

- In a meeting of government and New Korea Party officials on Thursday, Kim Kwang-il, Chief Secretary to the President, announced a decision to arrest all strike leaders as part of a tough policy against the strikes.

- The Seoul District Court on Thursday ordered top union leaders to present themselves for questioning today to decide about arrest warrants sought by prosecutors. Those summonsed include Kwon Young-kil, Chairman of the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions, and 19 other other union leaders.
